elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "Customer owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to ... all deliverables and work product created for Customer under this Agreement or any Exhibit"

elements.element: Vendor assigns deliverables/work product to Customer
elements.evidence: "Kubient hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to such deliverables and work product"
"Kubient retains all right, title and interest in the Auction Platform and its pre-existing and generally applicable technology, tools and know-how"

elements.element: Licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables (scope)
elements.evidence: "any Kubient materials embedded in such deliverables" — limited to "materials", not any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to Kubient any ownership interest in Customer Data or any other Customer intellectual property"
"no deliverable or Customer Data shall be jointly owned"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: "its pre-existing and generally applicable technology, tools and know-how"

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence in deliverables
elements.evidence: Customer takes outright ownership plus "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" to embedded Kubient materials

elements.element: Licence permits use, modification and sublicensing for Customer's business
elements.evidence: "to use, modify and sublicense ... for Customer's business purposes"

offending_extra_words: and Kubient may use Customer Data solely as necessary to provide the Services
reasons: Preferred embedded-IP licence is narrowed to "any Kubient materials embedded in such deliverables" rather than any Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables; widen the object of the licence to Vendor IP.
The insertion imports fallback-only rights ("worldwide", "modify and sublicense") into a preferred-level proposal, exceeding what is needed to complete the locked preferred position.

The added Vendor data-use grant ("Kubient may use Customer Data solely as necessary to provide the Services") is an unnecessary new licence to the counterparty and duplicates/undercuts the Customer Data retention sentence; it should be deleted.
The insertion is numbered "(b)" while the existing trademark/publicity paragraph is also "(b)", creating duplicate numbering and cross-reference ambiguity.
New undefined terms are introduced: "the Requests", "the Auction Platform" and "the Services" (the Agreement defines "Service"), creating a dangling definitional mechanic.
